brief: JPM's Prime Finance positioning wrap reports rising rates limited but did not derail equities this week, as AI optimism offset weakness elsewhere; overall positioning, flows and performance were little changed week-over-week, with net positioning still somewhat light and performance middling outside Quants. Hedge funds de-grossed globally (-0.6z), led by APAC (-1.7z) and a smaller US dip (-0.3z); net flows split by region, with strong Asia selling (>-2z), small EMEA buying, and flat North America. US positioning ticked up to the 40th percentile while EU slipped to the 17th. Rate-sensitive defensives kept getting sold: Utilities hit historical net-exposure lows (-2.5z) tracking the 10-year's rise, with Telecom also at historical lows and Real Estate near 12-month lows. Health Care crowding deteriorated further (L-S spread -7% over 5 days), driven by a deepening Clinical Biotech unwind (~2.4z sold over 20 days, ~12-month positioning lows) even as Commercial Biotech saw short covering. Financials showed buy-the-dip behavior (+2z), concentrated in Large Cap Banks and Insurance rather than Regionals. Tech re-risked, with Mag7 (~3z), Semis (+2z) and Software (+1z) bought and retail sentiment recovering toward average.
